knowledge-base.name: skill-routing
knowledge-base.triggers: suggest, next step, what to run, which skill, which command, proactive suggestion, routing, workflow guidance, what should I do next, what command
knowledge-base.overview:
Trigger-to-skill routing table. When a user's message or the current situation matches a trigger pattern below, append a short "What's next?" suggestion at the end of the response. This helps users discover the right ClaudeBoost skill without having to know the full catalog.
Rules (apply all four before suggesting): 1. One suggestion per response — don't stack multiple hints. 2. Phrase it as an option, not a command: "Consider running /review to..." not "Run /review now." 3. Skip if the user is already mid-skill (they're inside /qa, /workspace, /visualize, etc.). 4. Skip for trivial one-liners where a suggestion would feel patronizing.
Two suggestion surfaces — use the right format for each: 1. Mid-conversation proactive hint (inline, during a response): 1-2 sentences — "What's next: [skill] — [one-line reason why it fits here]." 2. Post-skill completion block (at the end of a /command file): a two-column table — "| If you... | Run |" with rows, placed after the final output section of the skill. Do not mix the formats. The sentence form belongs in responses; the table form belongs in command files.

triggers.signal: User describes a multi-step feature, epic, or initiative
More than ~5 files will be touched
User says: "I want to build X", "I need to implement Y", "we're starting on Z"
Ticket or PRD text is pasted

route.why: Creates an isolated workspace, plan, and agent routing map so the work stays organized across multiple sessions
route.sample: What's next: consider running /workspace to set up a structured plan before diving in — it routes you to the right agents and keeps state across sessions.

triggers.signal: User mentions working in an unfamiliar repo for the first time
User says: "I just cloned", "new project", "starting on this repo", "haven't worked in this before"
No project RAG index exists for the path

route.why: /index-project enables semantic codebase search; /research-project builds domain expertise about the stack and patterns before any code changes
route.sample: What's next: since this is a new codebase, run /index-project <path> to enable semantic search, then /research-project to build a stack overview before making changes.

triggers.signal: Task involves creating a new module, service, or subsystem
More than ~15 source files will be created
User says: "completely new", "new service", "new module", "greenfield", "rebuild"

route.why: Large initiatives need acceptance criteria and scope boundaries defined before implementation — a PRD prevents scope creep and gives agents a shared definition of done
route.sample: What's next: for a new subsystem this size, run /create-prd first to lock down scope and acceptance criteria, then /workspace to plan the build.

triggers.signal: User is exploring an unfamiliar library, API, or pattern
User says: "I'm not sure how X works", "haven't used this before", "researching", "figuring out"
Task has external dependencies the team hasn't used yet

route.why: Builds a curated knowledge base from relevant docs and sources; agents get those docs automatically via /context so they don't guess. /workspace must come first to create the workspace-id that /research-task requires.
route.sample: What's next: run /workspace to set up a plan, then /research-task [workspace-id] to index relevant docs — agents will pull from that knowledge automatically.

triggers.signal: User asks to explain, describe, or understand a system, flow, or component
User says: "how does X work", "explain the architecture", "show me the flow", "what connects to what"
An explanation is given that involves multiple components or layers

route.why: Turns a verbal explanation into an interactive diagram — much easier to reason about relationships and flows visually
route.sample: What's next: run /visualize to turn this into an interactive diagram — makes the relationships a lot easier to follow.

triggers.signal: User wants to understand which files/modules depend on each other
User says: "what calls this", "what imports this", "dependency graph", "what touches this file"

route.why: Builds a Files in Scope map using both vector and graph RAG seeded from the relevant entities — shows callers, importers, and inheritance chains
route.sample: What's next: run /graph [workspace-id] to map the dependency chain using both vector and structural RAG — it finds callers and importers you might miss with grep.

triggers.signal: User just wrote or modified code
A code change was committed or staged
User says: "just added", "I changed", "updated the code", "wrote this", "here's the implementation"

route.why: /review catches quality issues, logic errors, and standards violations; /qa verifies it works end-to-end in a real browser
route.sample: What's next: run /review to catch any issues, then /qa to verify the feature works end-to-end.

triggers.signal: User mentions authentication, authorization, secrets, tokens, or user input handling
Changes touch login, permissions, API keys, file uploads, or SQL queries
User says: "is this secure", "security review", "safe to ship", "auth"

route.why: Runs a focused OWASP-aware review on the pending branch changes — faster than a full /review when security is the primary concern
route.sample: What's next: run /security-review to check these changes for auth, injection, and data exposure issues before merging.

triggers.signal: User completed a significant piece of work and wants confidence it was done right
User says: "did I do this right", "check this", "is this correct", "verify this", "something feels off"
Multiple agents or steps were involved and the user wants a holistic sanity check

route.why: Runs a parallel multi-angle audit (security, quality, correctness, completeness) with an Opus verdict — independent of who did the work
route.sample: What's next: run /audit to get an independent parallel assessment — it checks security, quality, and correctness simultaneously.

triggers.signal: User says the feature is done, all tests pass, ready to merge
User says: "done", "ready to ship", "ready to merge", "finished", "all tests pass"

route.why: Runs a pre-push checklist (uncommitted changes, test status, branch hygiene) and pushes to remote when clean
route.sample: What's next: run /done to verify everything is clean and push to the remote.

triggers.signal: User wants to review a PR or someone else's code
User says: "review this PR", "look over this", "is this right", "check my colleague's code"

route.why: Runs a structured 15-pass parallel code review with an A-F grade — far more thorough than a manual read-through
route.sample: What's next: run /review --deep for a 15-pass parallel review with a letter grade and specific findings.

triggers.signal: User implemented a feature and wants to test it in a real browser
User says: "test this", "try it out", "run the tests", "does it work"
A local dev server is running or can be started

route.why: Runs a structured QA session with Playwright — discovers routes, executes journeys, captures screenshots, and writes a coverage gap report
route.sample: What's next: run /qa to exercise the feature in a real browser — it maps routes, runs journeys, and flags coverage gaps.

triggers.signal: User pastes a stack trace or error message
User says: "debug this", "why is X failing", "set a breakpoint", "step through", "step into", "trace this"
User asks: "what is the value of X at line Y", "why is this variable wrong"
User describes a runtime bug that needs live inspection
User says a process is crashing, hanging, or producing wrong output

route.why: Analyzes the error and traces root cause — static analysis for obvious bugs, live mcp-debugger step-through for runtime issues. Works across Python, .NET/ASP.NET, Go, Node.js, TypeScript, Java, and Rust.
route.sample: What's next: consider running /debug — it traces the root cause and can step through execution live with mcp-debugger to inspect runtime values at any line.

triggers.signal: Context window is above 70% full
User says: "context is getting long", "should we clear?", "starting to forget things"
Session has been running for a long time with many file reads

route.why: /clear-safe saves workspace state before clearing; /handoff writes a session summary so the next context window picks up exactly where this one left off
route.sample: What's next: run /clear-safe to save state, then /handoff to document the current progress before clearing — the next session will resume from where this one stopped.

triggers.signal: User wants to review what changed on the current branch
User says: "what did we change", "show me the diff", "what's been modified", "what's on this branch"

route.why: Interactive change explorer — shows everything modified on the current branch with file-level summaries
route.sample: What's next: run /changes to see an interactive summary of everything modified on this branch.

triggers.signal: User mentions slow queries, high latency, memory usage, or a bottleneck
User says: "slow", "performance", "optimize", "N+1", "memory leak", "taking too long"

route.why: Performance agent profiles bottlenecks, detects N+1 queries, and recommends caching strategies — specialized knowledge that the general context doesn't carry
route.sample: What's next: spawn performance-agent to profile the bottleneck — it has specific N+1 detection, query analysis, and caching strategy knowledge.

triggers.signal: User mentions missing logs, tracing, metrics, or monitoring gaps
User says: "add logging", "we can't see what's happening", "need metrics", "observability"

route.why: Observability agent applies the three-pillar strategy (logs/metrics/traces) and knows the project's logging standards to avoid both gaps and leakage
route.sample: What's next: spawn observability-agent to design a logging and metrics strategy — it applies the three-pillar model and project standards.

triggers.signal: User just ran /index-project successfully
Project RAG index was just created for the first time

route.why: Now that the codebase is indexed, /research-project builds a domain-expert summary of the stack, patterns, and conventions — agents get this context automatically
route.sample: What's next: run /research-project to build a stack overview — now that the codebase is indexed, this gives agents expert context about your project's patterns.

triggers.signal: Many files were added or modified since the last RAG index
RAG search is returning stale or irrelevant results
User says: "reindex", "RAG seems off", "update the index"

route.why: /index-boost reindexes ClaudeBoost's own knowledge bases; /index-project reindexes a project codebase — pick based on what changed
route.sample: What's next: run /index-boost if ClaudeBoost files changed, or /index-project <path> if project source files changed — keeps RAG results accurate.

triggers.signal: User wants to improve ClaudeBoost itself — new skill, agent tweak, knowledge file
User says: "improve this skill", "update the agent", "add a new command", "fix ClaudeBoost"

route.why: /self-improve runs an audit cycle that often surfaces related gaps; /workspace then plans the specific improvement with proper agent routing
route.sample: What's next: run /self-improve to check for related gaps first, then /workspace to plan the specific change.

triggers.signal: User wants to see how the session performed — tool calls, RAG usage, latency
User says: "how did that go", "session stats", "how many tool calls", "RAG usage"

route.why: Shows per-session tool call counts, RAG hit rates, DB breakdown, and latency — useful for spotting inefficiencies
route.sample: What's next: run /telemetry to see tool call counts, RAG usage, and latency for this session.

application-notes.note: This table is a guide, not a script. If none of the triggers fit cleanly, skip the suggestion.
If the user has already acknowledged a skill and chosen not to use it, don't suggest it again in the same session.
Suggestions work best right after a natural completion point — not mid-flow.
For the exact skill descriptions and arguments, see the skills listed in the session-primer or CLAUDE.md's "When to Use What" table.
